defect.problem: The good_law status survives, but the page/treatment presentation is too categorical if read as no negative-treatment risk at all. The lake record contains proposed negative/mentioned progeny edges and treatment derivation audit markers, so the safer disclosed-evidence statement is that no audited point override appears and the collective-knowledge rule is marked good_law.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep field_i_validity: good_law, but tighten the treatment note to: 'Marked good_law as to the collective-knowledge/probable-cause rule; no point overrides in the lake record. Proposed negative/mentioned progeny edges remain audit-needed.'

reasons: Lake treatment expressly says field_i_validity is good_law, varies_by_point is false, and point_overrides is empty.

The same lake treatment also lists proposed progeny edges with negative-looking field_ii labels and derivation lanes marked audit_needed/cap_hit, so a blanket no-negative-treatment phrasing is not fully secured by the disclosed record.
Because those edges are proposed and field_iii is only mentioned, they do not refute the good_law call itself.
residual_risks: A full CourtListener audit would be needed before retaining an unqualified 'No negative treatment' statement.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: State the treatment as good_law for the collective-knowledge/probable-cause rule, with no lake point overrides, rather than claiming categorical absence of negative treatment.
